hero.subtitle: If a crash on Route 49, Route 88, or one of the smaller Jackson streets has left you hurt, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney free of charge. There's no obligation and no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

about.title: Jackson Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Jackson sits at a crossroads of Route 49, Route 88, and their intersection, and even a small foothill town sees its share of collisions on these corridors. Public records show these crashes tend to cluster on Wednesday afternoons, often when traffic through town builds up. Whether your accident happened at the Rt 49/88 junction or on a quieter Amador County road, the aftermath is the same: medical bills, missed work, and calls from an insurance adjuster who doesn't work for you. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured Jackson residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Acting early matters here — evidence at rural intersections and along highway corridors can disappear quickly, and California's filing deadlines don't wait. We can help you get pointed in the right direction without any pressure or cost to start.

whyChoose.title: Why Jackson Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for a Route 49 or Route 88 collision, you can still recover a share of damages. An independent attorney can help make sure fault isn't unfairly pinned on you.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California places no cap on compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses in most car accident cases. That means your claim's value isn't artificially limited by state law.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to reduce or deny your claim. An independent attorney can advise you on what to say and when.

items.question: What if my crash happened at the Route 49/88 intersection and there's no police report yet?
items.answer: Even without a completed police report, evidence like photos, witness contact information, and vehicle damage should be preserved as soon as possible. Physical evidence at busy Jackson intersections can be cleared or altered quickly. An attorney can help gather and document what's needed for your claim.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and there's no cost to have your situation reviewed. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, so you don't pay unless they recover compensation for you.
